payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the source mug visibly positioned to the right of the same headphones in the edited image; if not, is there reliable visual evidence of relevant attempted movement of the source mug, or reliable evidence that no relevant progress occurred?
node.criteria: Pass only when visual evidence reliably establishes that the source mug itself is now positioned to the right of the same headphones. Fail when visual evidence reliably establishes either that relevant attempted movement occurred without fulfillment, or that no relevant progress toward the requested move occurred. For attempted movement, assess the source mug's former location and surrounding edited scene together; a conspicuous remnant or other visible changes may support attempted movement even if the right-side mug's identity cannot be established. Do not infer source-mug identity or fulfillment from color alone, from a mug being on the right, or from unrelated/newly generated mugs. A remnant counts as evidence of attempted movement only when its shape, position, and appearance reliably connect it to the source mug or otherwise clearly indicate a relevant edit. Use unknown when evidence cannot reliably establish fulfillment, attempted movement, or absence of progress. High confidence in uncertainty is not evidence that the requested edit is absent.
node.binding: Compare the source image's large light-blue mug, including its body and handle, with the edited mugs, allowing for changes in appearance, scale, and lighting; compare the same headphones and assess whether the source mug is to their right. Separately inspect the source mug's former location and surrounding edited scene for reliable evidence of attempted movement, including the remnant's position, outline, and appearance and any other visible changes. Do not treat color alone, an indistinct blur, or a different-looking mug as proof of source-mug identity or progress. Keep attempted movement distinct from fulfillment: attempted movement without fulfillment is fail for this required condition; retain unknown if neither fulfillment nor relevant progress/no-progress can reliably be established.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows the same headphones near the center and a mug to their right, but that mug is small and white, unlike the source's large light-blue mug, so its identity is not established. At the source mug's former left-side location there is a conspicuous light-blue, mug-shaped blur/remnant, while the original mug is absent there. Together these visible changes reliably indicate an attempted move, but do not establish that the source mug itself is now to the headphones' right.

Make the decision output/criterion explicitly distinguish fulfillment, reliable attempted movement without fulfillment, reliable absence of progress, and unresolved evidence, then ensure the aggregate maps the observed attempted-move case to partial rather than treating this single requirement’s fail as overall no. Preserve that evidence without treating color alone as identity. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; the mismatch is in decision-to-aggregate semantics, not missing visual evidence."}
